rounds.proof_sketch: cols=4000, blockDim.x=256. Thread tid=160 iterates i=160,416,...,3744,4000. With `i<=cols`, thread 160 executes one extra iteration at i=4000, writing shared[4000]=input[row*4000+4000]. However: (1) shared memory is allocated for exactly 4000 floats, so shared[4000] is OOB but doesn't corrupt used indices 0-3999; (2) the sequential scan only processes shared[0..3999]; (3) the store loop uses `i<cols`, writing only shared[0..3999] to output. The infected location shared[4000] is never read.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the load loop condition from `i < cols` to `i <= cols`, causing thread 160 (since 4000 = 160 + 15*256) to execute one additional iteration writing to shared[4000]. This is an out-of-bounds write to shared memory, but critically, this location is never subsequently read. The sequential scan processes only indices 1 through cols-1 (i.e., 1 to 3999). The store loop uses the original `i < cols` condition, so only shared[0] through shared[3999] are written to output. The mutated code produces identical outputs because the corruption occurs in memory that doesn't participate in the output computation. This is a classic infection-no-propagation scenario where the mutation executes different code but the state difference never reaches observable outputs.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation writes to shared[4000] which is never read. No value-level variation can cause this write to affect output. The store loop uses `i < cols` (unmutated), so indices 0-3999 are written to output, and these values are computed correctly regardless of the mutated load condition.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing GPU kernels, track which mutations affect only dead writes or out-of-bounds locations that don't feed into outputs. The mutation testing framework should detect that shared[cols] is never read in subsequent code paths, flagging this as an 'infection-no-propagation' equivalent mutant. Consider adding static analysis to identify mutations to loop bounds where the extra/missing iterations write to locations not consumed by later computation.
